title: Robust enhanced index tracking portfolio selection under distributional uncertainty
data_sources: Yahoo! Finance monthly adjusted closing prices January 2015 to December 2024 for 25 tickers listed
sample: 25 U.S. stocks: 5 largest by market capitalization from each of 5 sectors - Technology (AAPL, NVDA, MSFT, AVGO, ORCL), Healthcare (JNJ, ABBV, LLY, UNH, ABT), Financial Services (BRK-B, JPM, V, BAC, MA), Consumer Cyclical (AMZN, TSLA, HD, MCD, BKNG), Consumer Defensive (WMT, COST, KO, PG, PM). Monthly loss data from Yahoo! Finance. In-sample training 60-month rolling window; out-of-sample evaluation 60 months. Short-selling allowed (W=R^n) and prohibited (W=A^n, omega>=0) regimes reported separately. Uncertainty sets M_{n+1}(mu,Sigma) and D_{n+1}(gamma1,gamma2) evaluated separately.
method: 1. Universe: select 25 stocks as 5 largest market-cap per 5 sectors listed above.

2. Data: download monthly adjusted closing price P_{i,t} from Yahoo! Finance for January 2015 to December 2024. Compute monthly loss x_{i,t}=-(P_{i,t+1}-P_{i,t})/P_{i,t}; return is -x_{i,t}; vector x_t=(x_{1,t},...,x_{25,t}).

3. Parameters: set alpha=-0.04 (-alpha=0.04 excess over index), r0=0.02 (M_{n+1} minimum expected return), r=-0.01 (D_{n+1} minimum worst-case expected return), kappa=5 (kappa0=4.65 lower bound for M-ER existence requiring kappa>kappa0 where kappa0=(2+2*sqrt(b0+1))/b0), gamma1=0.22 and gamma2=0.025 (D_{n+1} size; figure captions also print gamma1=0.21). Empirical calibrations: -bar(alpha)=0.0075 average historical excess over index, bar(r)=0.0176 average portfolio return from in-sample data. Window =60 months (5 years).

4. Estimation: for each out-of-sample month t=1..60 (January 2020 to December 2024), estimate mu_hat and Sigma_hat from preceding 60-month window. For D_{n+1}, calibrate gamma1,gamma2 via rolling 60-month windows: gamma1_i=(mu_hat_{n,i}-mu_hat_n)' Sigma_hat_n^{-1} (mu_hat_{n,i}-mu_hat_n), gamma2_i=||Sigma_hat_i - Sigma_hat||_F; set gamma1,gamma2 to averages of gamma1_i,gamma2_i.

5. Optimization: solve M-ER, ER, M-TSV, TSV, M-V, V models. Under M_{n+1}(mu,Sigma) use closed-form solutions Theorem 1 and Proposition 1 (m=1 ER and m=2 TSV) and solutions for MV (1) and V (2) with omega in R^n. Under D_{n+1}(gamma1,gamma2) solve equivalent convex SOCP problems (3)-(6) with/without constraint omega>=0. Also compute equal-weighted portfolio EWP (1/n).

6. Backtest: initial optimal portfolio omega0* from January 2015-December 2019 training data; out-of-sample return R_t= -omega_{t-1}* ' * x_t for t=1..60 rolling window forward by one month each step.

7. Performance metrics: compute out-of-sample cumulative wealth CW, mean return, standard deviation SD, expected regret ER=E[(omega'X - X0 - alpha)_+], target semi-variance TSV=E[(omega'X - X0 - alpha)_+^2], Sharpe ratio, Sortino ratio, Omega ratio as defined in cited references. Report Table M (M_{n+1}) and Table D (D_{n+1}) with/without short selling; best per criterion boxed. Plot CW and ratios versus kappa to assess sensitivity and locate optima.
